content:
Let adjacency mean the 17-cycle \(C_{17}\). Connective permutations are exactly the automorphisms of \(C_{17}\), i.e. rotations or reflections.

For an adjacent pair \(e\), consider its orbit under powers of \(p\). For \(1\le j<N\), \(p^j\) is dispersive, so \(p^j(e)\) is not an adjacent pair. Since \(p^N\) is connective, \(p^N(e)\) is an adjacent pair.

Thus the only adjacent pairs in the orbit of \(e\) are \(e\) itself and possibly \(p^N(e)\). The orbit size is \(N\) if \(p^N(e)=e\), and \(2N\) otherwise. Hence each edge orbit contains either one edge and has size \(N\), or contains two edges and has size \(2N\).

There are \(17\) edges in \(C_{17}\). If \(r\) edge orbits have one edge and \(s\) have two edges, then
\[
r+2s=17.
\]
The total number of unordered pairs in these edge orbits is
\[
rN+s(2N)=N(r+2s)=17N.
\]
This cannot exceed the total number of unordered pairs of residues,
\[
\binom{17}{2}=136.
\]
So
\[
17N\le 136 \implies N\le 8.
\]

Now construct \(N=8\). Take
\[
p(x)=3x \pmod{17}.
\]
The number \(3\) has order \(16\) modulo \(17\), so for \(1\le j\le 7\),
\[
3^j\not\equiv \pm1 \pmod{17}.
\]
Thus if \(x,y\) are adjacent, then \(x-y\equiv \pm1\), so
\[
p^j(x)-p^j(y)\equiv 3^j(x-y)\equiv \pm 3^j\not\equiv \pm1,
\]
meaning \(p^j\) is dispersive for \(j=1,\dots,7\).

For \(j=8\),
\[
3^8\equiv -1\pmod{17},
\]
so
\[
p^8(x)\equiv -x \pmod{17},
\]
which is a reflection of the 17-cycle, hence connective.

Therefore the largest possible value is

\[
\boxed{8}.
\]
